text: The Sun contains about 99.86% of the mass in the solar system.
Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun and has a very thin atmosphere, causing extreme temperature changes.
Venus has a thick, toxic atmosphere and surface temperatures hot enough to melt lead — it's the hottest planet in the solar system.
Humans once landed probes on the surface of Venus, the most notable being Venera 13.

text.text: Earth is the only known planet with liquid water on its surface and life as we know it.
Earth is the 3rd planet from the sun, taking 365 days to orbit it!
The Moon is about 1/4 the diameter of Earth, which is why lunar eclipses still cover the Sun from our view.
A day on Mars (a 'sol') is about 24 hours and 39 minutes — very close to an Earth day.
Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system and its Great Red Spot is a storm larger than Earth.
Saturn is famous for its beautiful rings, made mostly of ice and rock.
Uranus rotates on its side, likely because of a huge collision early in its history.
Neptune has the strongest winds in the solar system, reaching over 1,200 mph in some storms.
Pluto is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt; it was reclassified in 2006
The universe has been expanding since the Big Bang about 13.8 billion years ago.
